name: Posterior thalamic radiation
summary: The posterior thalamic radiation connects the pulvinar and the lateral posterior nucleus with the parietal and occipital association cortex, running through the retrolenticular part of the internal capsule lateral to the atrium of the lateral ventricle, alongside and mixed with the optic radiation. It carries the thalamic contribution to visual attention, spatial perception and the integration of vision with somatosensation, and lesions of this region combine field defects from the optic radiation with neglect, visuospatial disorganization and, on the left, alexia and agraphia. The stratum sagittale that contains it is the corridor for the posterior cerebral and middle cerebral artery watershed and a common site of periventricular leukomalacia and of glioma spread.

anatomy.location: From the pulvinar and lateral posterior nucleus backward and laterally through the retrolenticular internal capsule into the stratum sagittale lateral to the atrium and the occipital horn, fanning to the posterior parietal cortex, the angular gyrus, the lateral occipital cortex and the posterior temporal cortex.

efferents.to: Posterior parietal, angular and lateral occipital cortex

function: The pulvinar receives the superior colliculus, the visual cortex and the parietal cortex and uses this bundle to coordinate attention across the visual field, to bind the features of an attended object and to suppress distracters; the lateral posterior nucleus contributes to the spatial and reaching functions of the superior parietal lobule; and corticothalamic fibers return through it from the parietal and occipital cortex. Because it shares the stratum sagittale with the optic radiation, its lesions add attentional and perceptual deficits to a hemianopia, and disconnection of the pulvinar from the parietal cortex on the right is one of the mechanisms of neglect. It is also the route by which the thalamus reaches the visual word form and angular gyrus regions on the left.

bestView.label: posterior thalamic radiation from the pulvinar to the parieto-occipital cortex
retrolenticular fibers lateral to the atrium

imaging.normalAppearance: Tractography shows a posterior bundle from the pulvinar through the retrolenticular capsule into the parieto-occipital white matter, overlapping the optic radiation; on T2 the stratum sagittale lateral to the atrium contains both.

pathology.finding: Restricted diffusion in the parieto-occipital white matter lateral to the atrium with hemianopia, neglect or visuospatial impairment.
Loss of the peritrigonal white matter in ex-premature children with visual perceptual difficulty and field defects.

pathology.pathology: Glioma spreading along the stratum sagittale
pathology.finding: FLAIR-bright infiltration of the peritrigonal white matter extending between the temporal, parietal and occipital lobes.

lesionEffects.deficit: Contralateral neglect and impaired visual attention (right)
lesionEffects.mechanism: Disconnection of the pulvinar from the parietal attention cortex
Loss of the lateral posterior-parietal projection
Involvement of the accompanying optic radiation

examination: Line bisection, cancellation and extinction testing
Reading and writing when the left side is involved
pearls: Peritrigonal lesions take away both the seeing and the noticing: hemianopia plus neglect
The pulvinar is the thalamus of attention; its radiation is the wire
Periventricular leukomalacia damages this radiation early, which is why ex-premature children have perceptual visual problems
